ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: FullMath.mulDiv() → blocked by: 512-bit phantom overflow protection → verdict: no extraction path
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: mulDiv uses Chinese Remainder Theorem with 512-bit intermediate. Tested with max inputs (type(uint256).max). mulDivRoundingUp >= mulDiv proven symbolically by Halmos.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: SwapMath.computeSwapByInputStep() → blocked by: fee deduction before swap + rounding UP → verdict: no free tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee deducted first via mulDiv(amount, MAX_BPS - fee, MAX_BPS). Remaining goes to swap. Output <= input at any price. Tested with fee=0, fee=9999, fee=10000, amountRemaining=1. Fuzz with 25+ runs.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick/getTickAtSqrtPrice → blocked by: exact round-trip at all ticks → verdict: no tick-price desync
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Round-trip tested: tick -> price -> tick at every 1000th tick from MIN_TICK to MAX_TICK. Also fuzz-tested with 25+ random ticks. All exact.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromInput/Output → blocked by: FullMath + correct rounding directions → verdict: price always moves correctly
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Halmos: check_priceMovesCorrectDirection explored 31 paths, no counterexample (timeout). Forge: tested at MIN_SQRT_RATIO, MAX_SQRT_RATIO, zero amount. Price decreases for zeroForOne, increases for !zeroForOne.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta/getAmount1Delta → blocked by: roundUp >= roundDown proven symbolically → verdict: rounding favors protocol
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Halmos: check_deltaRoundingDirection explored 68 paths (timeout). Forge fuzz: 5000 runs in InvariantMathProperties, all pass. roundUp always >= roundDown for both amount0 and amount1.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: DynamicHelper._getTokensOwed() uint128 truncation → blocked by: requires >1e20 swaps for truncation → verdict: practically unreachable
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: uint128(FullMath.mulDiv(delta, liquidity, Q128)) truncates if result > uint128.max. With realistic liquidity (1e18), need delta > 1.16e59 — requires ~1e23 swaps. With minimum liquidity (1), max delta of uint256.max gives exactly uint128.max (no truncation). Proven in test_D2.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: DynamicHelper._crossTick() fee growth wrapping → blocked by: unchecked modular arithmetic by design (Uniswap V3 pattern) → verdict: correct
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeGrowthOutside subtraction wraps by design. Double flip restores original value. _getFeeGrowthInside uses same unchecked pattern — modular arithmetic cancels out wrapping. Standard Uniswap V3 design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: BitMath.mostSignificantBit/leastSignificantBit → blocked by: De Bruijn lookup table proven correct → verdict: no extraction path
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Halmos: check_msbOfPowerOf2 PASS (MSB(2^n) = n for all n). Forge: tested all 256 powers of 2, MSB/LSB consistency fuzz, revert on 0 input. Slither incorrect-shift is false positive for De Bruijn pattern.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: LiquidityMath.addDelta() → blocked by: assembly overflow check via shr(128, z) → verdict: safe
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Halmos: check_noUnderflow tested (expectRevert unsupported but paths explored). Forge fuzz: 25 runs testing all overflow/underflow cases. Edge: int128.min + uint128(2^127) = 0 correctly.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: FeeHelper input/output fee asymmetry → blocked by: input allows 100% fee (correct for input path), output rejects 100% (prevents div-by-zero) → verdict: intentional design
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Input: fee = mulDivRoundingUp(amount, feeBPS, MAX_BPS), allows feeBPS=10000. Output: fee = mulDivRoundingUp(reserve, feeBPS, MAX_BPS - feeBPS), reverts when feeBPS >= MAX_BPS (div by 0). protocolFee never exceeds lpFee (proven by fuzz). Unchecked subtraction at L223 is safe.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput() rounds UP taker output → blocked by: max extraction 2 wei per fill → verdict: dust-level, not exploitable
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB uses mulDivRoundingUp twice for output, giving taker up to 2 wei more per fill vs exact math. Over 10000 fills: max extraction 20000 wei (<$0.01 for any real token). Gas cost of fills far exceeds extraction. SingleProviderHelper correctly uses mulDiv (rounds DOWN).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96() overflow → blocked by: returns 0 on overflow, MIN_SQRT_RATIO prevents zero-price swaps → verdict: Cetus pattern blocked
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96(type(uint256).max, 1) returns 0. But MIN_SQRT_RATIO = 4295128739 prevents any swap at price 0. Pool creation validates sqrtPrice >= MIN_SQRT_RATIO. Cetus-style overflow attack not possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: Balancer rounding direction dust loop → blocked by: all divisions round against user → verdict: protocol keeps dust
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 1000 sequential 1-wei add/remove operations: protocol gains dust every round (roundUp for deposit, roundDown for withdrawal). 1000 sequential 1-wei swaps: pool never loses value. Fee rounding: input fee uses mulDivRoundingUp (takes more from user).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: ERC-4626 first depositor inflation on DynamicPoolType → blocked by: no share/asset conversion — each position tracks independent liquidity → verdict: not applicable
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Dynamic pool positions track individual liquidity amounts, not shares. No global share token exists to dilute. First depositor with liquidity=1 cannot inflate anything. ERC-4626 inflation attack pattern does not apply to concentrated liquidity design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: Hook price manipulation via extreme sqrtPriceX96 → blocked by: MIN_SQRT_RATIO/MAX_SQRT_RATIO bounds + TickMath validation → verdict: extreme prices handled safely
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: getNextSqrtPriceFromInput works correctly at MIN_SQRT_RATIO+1 and MAX_SQRT_RATIO-1. Price=0 reverts. TickMath validates sqrtPrice range. No bypass found for hook-injected extreme prices.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: INV-SW02 profitable round-trip → blocked by: fees + rounding both go against user → verdict: no profitable round-trip
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz tested: swap A->B then B->A with random amounts and fees (26 runs dynamic, 25 runs fixed). Output always <= input. Fees + rounding both extract from user. No counterexample found.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: Fee=10000 BPS (100%) edge case value leak → blocked by: 100% fee routes all input to fee, 0 output → verdict: no value leak
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: With fee=10000: amountRemainingLessFee = mulDiv(amount, 0, 10000) = 0, so amountIn=0, feeAmount=full amount, amountOut=0. Tested with 1e18 and type(uint128).max inputs. No value created.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: Price manipulation via repeated tiny swaps → blocked by: fee rounds up to 1 wei, consuming entire input → verdict: price cannot be moved cheaply
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: With 0.3% fee and 1 wei input: fee = mulDiv(1, 30, 10000) = 0, but fee is mulDivRoundingUp so fee = 1 = full input. amountRemainingLessFee = 0. 100 sequential 1-wei swaps: price unchanged, 0 output, all input goes to fees.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: FeeHelper output fee unchecked subtraction (L223) → blocked by: protocolFee <= lpFee always (mulDiv(lpFee, protocolBPS, MAX_BPS) <= lpFee) → verdict: no underflow
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: protocolFeeAmount = mulDiv(lpFeeAmount, protocolBPS, 10000). Since protocolBPS <= 10000, result <= lpFeeAmount. Fuzz tested with 25 runs across all fee/protocolFee combinations. Even 100% protocolFee: result = lpFee (safe subtraction to 0).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: target: SingleProviderHelper.calculateFixedInput/Output round-trip → blocked by: mulDiv (roundDown) for input, mulDivRoundingUp for output → verdict: always loses on round-trip
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: calculateFixedInput uses mulDiv (rounds DOWN output = user gets less). calculateFixedOutput uses mulDivRoundingUp (rounds UP input = user pays more). Both directions lose. Fuzz: 25 runs in both directions, no profit.

theft_theses.thesis: CLOB calculateFixedInput rounds UP taker output, systematically overpaying takers at maker expense
theft_theses.asset: Order tokens (up to 2 wei per fill)

theft_theses.thesis: _getTokensOwed uint128 truncation silently discards LP fees above uint128.max
SwapMath fee=10000 edge case creates tokens from nothing
Repeated tiny swaps move price without paying proper fees (oracle manipulation)
FeeHelper output fee unchecked subtraction underflows when protocolFee > lpFee
